text.p: Chaparral Resources Inc said Thursday $1.1 million in financing has been obtained, primarily for its Kazakhstan venture.

Chaparral said the interim financing was through three 18.5-month convertible promissory notes that bear interest at eight percent per annum. The notes are convertible into Chaparral common at the lower of $0.75 per share or 75 percent of the common's market price if that is less than $1 on the date of the conversion.
Also, the company said, it has an oral commitment for an additional $250,000 of such financing.

In addition, the company said, it has agreed to issue to the lenders three-year warrants to purchase a total of 337,500 common shares at $0.25 per share, and agreed to add two directors selected by the lenders to the company's board. As part of this change in the board, James A. Jeffs, a current director, has resigned.

Warrants to purchase an additional 135,000 and 270,000 shares at $0.25 per share will have to be issued if the promissory notes are not paid or converted by May 31, 1997, and November 30, 1997, respectively.

The funds are to be used primarily for the Karakuduk project and for corporate operations, Chapparral said, noting it is required to provide the financing for the Karakuduk Munay Inc Joint Venture. The company controls a 50 percent beneficial ownership interest in the venture and the field. The other 50 percent is held by a Kazakhstan regional government group. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
